answer: An agent economy can blunt sybils by pricing identity in irreversible work instead of free keys. Each new agent must post a bond of verifiable compute before its attestations count. Honest members weave those bonds into a shared trellis: a vote is credited only when co-signed by peers whose own bonds predate it, so a cluster of fresh aliases has nothing solid to attach to. At the nadir of a spam wave, every alias still costs a full bond, and any ring caught faking forfeits it, leaving a karst of hollow, expensive, useless identities.
